Scroll direction, :target-before and rounded polygon()

I wanted to see how three newer CSS features behave when they drive a 2D drawable canvas. Scroll the article below to fold its toolbar with @container scroll-state(scrolled) and zero scroll listeners, swipe the carousel to fan cards from :target-before and :target-after, then drag the clipped card to tilt a polygon(round ...) silhouette and its shadow.

01 · scroll-state

Scroll down to fold the toolbar

This scroller carries container-type: scroll-state. Scrolling down sets scrolled: bottom and transitions --hide to 1.

02 · live controls

The search box filters these notes

Type a word like "shadow" or "fan" into the toolbar above when it is open. The DOM inside the canvas filters these cards in place.

03 · zero scroll listeners

No scroll handler is attached here

Scrolling this drawable child changes its picture and fires the canvas paint event. The script reads --hide and folds the toolbar in two hinged halves.

04 · registered property

@property --hide interpolates cleanly

Because --hide is registered as a number, Chrome transitions it smoothly between 0 and 1 so the canvas draws the intermediate fold angles.

05 · scroll back up

Reverse direction to unfold it

Flick back towards the top and @container scroll-state(scrolled: top) returns --hide to 0. Once flat, the toolbar takes taps and typing again.

06 · focus safety

Hidden toolbars turn inert

When the toolbar is folded past 60%, the script marks it inert so keyboard Tab navigation skips controls you cannot see.

07 · fallback controls

Works with manual toggles too

If your browser does not parse scroll-state(scrolled) yet, use the Simulate buttons below the canvas to drive the same --hide transition.

:target-before and :target-after carousel fan

This horizontal list uses scroll-snap-type, ::scroll-marker and ::scroll-button(). The CSS rules for :target-before, :target-current and :target-after style the dots and set --fan-side and --fan-tilt on each marker. The 2D canvas reads those properties to tilt passed cards left, centre the active card and stack upcoming cards on the right. Every card holds a live Pin button and Lock checkbox.

Rounded polygon(round ...) clip paths on drawn cards

Switch between four clip shapes and move the corner-radius slider, then drag across the card to tilt it. Because drawElementImage() preserves transparent pixels outside the card's CSS clip-path, the 2D canvas shadow follows the notched or rounded outline rather than a rectangle.

How it works

  • In the first demo, #s1-scroller carries container-type: scroll-state and is a drawable child of the canvas. When you scroll it, its painted pixels change and Chrome fires the canvas paint event without any scroll listener. A probe inside the scroller matches @container scroll-state(scrolled: bottom) or top and transitions --hide. The paint handler reads --hide via getComputedStyle() and draws #s1-toolbar either flat (for exact hit testing when open) or split across two clipped, shaded accordion panels.
  • In the second demo, #f2-deck is a drawable child that holds the horizontal snap list, generated ::scroll-button() arrows and ::scroll-marker dots. Each card is a nested drawable child positioned against the deck so the scroller never clips its picture. On every paint, the script reads --fan-side and --fan-tilt from getComputedStyle(stop, '::scroll-marker') and draws the passed cards tilted left, the upcoming cards stacked right and the current card last on top.
  • In the third demo, the card's CSS clip-path punches transparent pixels outside the polygon in the element picture. Canvas 2D shadows (shadowColor, shadowBlur, shadowOffsetX, shadowOffsetY) trace the non-transparent alpha of drawElementImage(), so the shadow automatically follows notches, chevrons and rounded corners. When a browser doesn't parse polygon(round ...) yet, the canvas builds a matching arcTo() path for the shadow and clip so the radius slider stays usable.

Live checks

Each check builds its own isolated fixture on the test stage and reads pixels from a plain 2D copy canvas. Nothing touches the three demos above.

ResultExperimentDetail

Findings

Browser support for scroll-state(scrolled), :target-before/:target-after and polygon(round ...) varies across Chrome 130 to 160. The live checks table above reports what your browser does right now.

  • Scroll direction without scroll listeners: scrolling a drawable 2D child updates its picture and raises paint on the canvas. Pairing that with @container scroll-state(scrolled: bottom) and a registered @property --hide lets the canvas fold a live toolbar without touching the scroll event.
  • Hit testing during a split draw: when a drawable element is drawn in two clipped halves to fake an accordion crease, the second drawElementImage() call overwrites the hit box. Drawing the toolbar in one call once --hide <= 0.01 restores exact hit boxes, and marking it inert past 60% folded keeps hidden inputs out of Tab order.
  • Reading custom properties from ::scroll-marker: getComputedStyle(slide, '::scroll-marker').getPropertyValue('--fan-side') lets the canvas inspect :target-before, :target-current and :target-after directly in CSS. When a browser lacks those pseudo-classes, falling back to scrollLeft keeps the fan working.
  • Clipped alpha and canvas shadows: clip-path: polygon(...) is baked into the element's picture before drawElementImage() receives it, so 2D drop shadows follow the clipped polygon outline.
  • Not verified here: real touch fling behaviour, Chrome 159 on Android and exact Chrome milestone rollout for polygon(round ...) in a headless run. See findings/scroll-directions.md for the full record.
